description:
Earth moves in silence. Clouds hide it—radar doesn't.

I'm Rajeev (CSE @ MUJ, AIML Tech Lead, Top 1% IITM AI/DS). I build with Python, MySQL, and AI to turn unseen signals into interactive tools. For Dancing with the SARs, I'm decoding NASA-ISRO NISAR data to reveal India's shifting waters and land.

Solo mission. Not recruiting—just building until launch
summary:
NISAR-PULSE is an open-source, interactive web application that transforms NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) observations into an accessible time-series explorer and physical-driver interpreter.

To address the Dancing with the SARs challenge, the application analyzes multi-date SAR backscatter across HH and HV polarizations to isolate shifts in surface roughness and dielectric constant. Through a split-screen before/after slider, polarization toggles, and a guided Story Mode, users can investigate two contrasting Indian regions: monsoon flood inundation and crop-moisture shifts in the Krishna River Delta (Vijayawada), and seasonal wetland contraction and ground movement around Sambhar Salt Lake (Jaipur).

Optical satellites fail under heavy monsoon clouds when communities need data most. Because radar penetrates clouds day and night, NISAR-Pulse turns complex satellite telemetry into actionable insights for disaster responders, farmers, and researchers.

NAMASTE AND HELLO!!!
LIVE PROJECT & DEMO LINKS (NO LOGIN REQUIRED):

  • Live Orbital SAR Command Center (Web App): https://devcraftlab07-byte.github.io/nisar-pulse/
  • 7-Slide Global Judging Presentation Deck:https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1wiCuKING__fpXRBtuXDZ8C0-9bA3AMrQ/edit?usp=sharing
  • Interactive Story & Slide Demo Portal (Google Sites):https://sites.google.com/view/nisar-pulse-demo
  • Open-Source Code & Python NISAR Pipeline (GitHub):https://github.com/devcraftlab07-byte/nisar-pulse

THE MISSION: SEEING THROUGH THE MONSOON BLIND SPOT When peak monsoon cyclones hit India, optical satellites (Landsat, Sentinel-2) are 100% blinded by thick cloud cover and nightfall—precisely when emergency teams and farmers need surface data most. Meanwhile, NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) penetrates clouds day and night, but its Level-2 GCOV products ship inside complex multidimensional HDF5 covariance cubes that local decision-makers cannot easily read.

NISAR-Pulse bridges that gap: an open-source, zero-install spatial cockpit and Python data pipeline that translates dual-band L-band (24 cm) and S-band (9.4 cm) radar physics into real-time flood, soil-moisture, and ground-motion intelligence.

HOW IT WORKS (THREE-STAGE ARCHITECTURE)

  1. Automated Ingestion (Python + asf_search + h5py): Queries calibrated NISAR Level-2 GCOV (Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance) HDF5 granules from NASA's ASF DAAC and extracts HHHH (co-polarized surface bounce) and HVHV (cross-polarized canopy volume) matrices alongside Level-3 Vegetation Water Content (VWC).
    • Specular Flood Inundation (HH drop < -3.0 dB): Calm floodwater acts as a mirror, reflecting radar pulses away from the sensor.
    • Dielectric Soil Moisture Surge (HH rise > +2.0 dB): Saturated soils drive permittivity (epsilon) up to ~78.4, amplifying surface return.
    • Canopy Biomass Volume (HV gain): Growing crop stalks depolarize radar waves, lifting cross-polarized HV return (+5.6 dB).
  2. Interactive Spatial Cockpit: Streams processed layers into a 60fps WebGL/Canvas command center featuring a 3D orbital Earth with atmospheric Fresnel shaders, a synchronized Before/After SAR split-screen comparator, live Delta_sigma_0 classification sliders, an audio-reactive LFM chirp oscilloscope, and a 1-click GeoJSON vector mask exporter.

GROUNDED INDIAN CASE STUDIES & INTENDED IMPACT

  • Study Site 01 — Krishna River Delta & Vijayawada Basin, Andhra Pradesh (16.51 N, 80.65 E): Uses 24 cm L-band waves to penetrate storm clouds and dense rice canopies across 120 km of coastline and 50–75% alluvial clay soils—pinpointing 364 sq km of sub-canopy flood inundation (-6.8 dB HH drop) for disaster routing and crop insurance verification.
  • Study Site 02 — Sambhar Salt Lake & Jaipur Rim, Rajasthan (26.94 N, 75.08 E): Uses extreme dielectric contrast between hypersaline brine (epsilon ~79.2) and dry salt crusts across a 230 sq km Ramsar wetland (5,700 sq km catchment), paired with multi-pass L-band InSAR phase fringes to flag centimeter-scale groundwater subsidence bowls before irreversible aquifer compaction occurs.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

  • Data & Science Pipeline: Python 3, NASA asf_search API, h5py, NumPy, GeoJSON.
  • Frontend & Spatial Engine: HTML5, JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js / WebGL (custom GLSL Fresnel atmospheric shader & orbital mechanics), 2D Canvas API, Tailwind CSS, Web Audio API (LFM radar chirp synthesizer).
  • Presentation & Hosting: GitHub Pages, Google Sites, and a 7-slide executive deck.

WHY NISAR-PULSE STANDS OUT (CREATIVITY & DESIGN FACTORS) Rather than showing static satellite plots, NISAR-Pulse turns microwave remote sensing into a living exploratory instrument. Judges and users can click "LAUNCH MISSION BRIEFING" for an automated cinematic fly-through of both Indian basins, toggle simulated monsoon clouds to see optical failure vs. SAR penetration first-hand, adjust decibel thresholds to watch flood and moisture polygons recalculate in real time, and export ready-to-use GeoJSON boundaries for local GIS teams.
Thank You and May You Have A Nice Day Ahead
